description: Compact Ascend operator-development decision patterns. They ask Codex to make and justify decisions without prescribing fixed implementation parameters.

patterns.title: Freeze the platform-visible contract
patterns.decide: Record entrypoint, inputs/outputs/attrs, optionality/defaults, dtype/shape/mode semantics, required files and target CANN/SOC from authoritative sources.
patterns.guardrails: Do not invent missing semantics or expose scheduling choices as new public inputs.
patterns.validate: Compare registration/host/kernel assumptions with the task statement and current official template/package.

patterns.title: Enumerate the legal domain and keep Host metadata consistent
patterns.decide: Record legal ranks, shapes, dtypes, modes and optionals, and ensure output shape/dtype inference plus launch setup describe exactly what the kernel produces.
patterns.guardrails: Visible cases are not the whole domain unless the contract says so; Host and Kernel must not implement divergent mode logic.
patterns.validate: Exercise shape/launch setup at every mode/rank/optional boundary.

patterns.title: Define one truth model for overlapping mode signals
patterns.decide: Choose the semantic source of truth and agreement rule when shape, attrs or optional inputs encode the same mode.
patterns.guardrails: Do not infer precedence/defaults from names.
patterns.validate: Cover every legal mode and any required disagreement/absent-optional behavior.

patterns.title: Write the mathematical stage/dependency graph before tiling
patterns.decide: Identify reads, reductions/statistics, intermediates, persistent state and output dependencies, then decide which stages are separate or fused.
patterns.guardrails: Hardware convenience must not change masks, reduction domains, recurrence order or output semantics.
patterns.validate: Map each kernel stage back to contract equations/reference behavior.

patterns.title: Share one semantic core across fixed/varlen/tail variants when practical
patterns.decide: Hide offset/layout/chunk differences behind helpers or tiling metadata when the algorithm is the same.
patterns.guardrails: Split paths only for a real algorithm/resource difference, not convenience alone.
patterns.validate: Check equivalent fixed/varlen boundaries and state/output indexing.

patterns.title: Separate dependency axes from parallel axes and assign task ownership
patterns.decide: Mark each logical axis independent, reduction-coupled, recurrence-coupled or producer-consumer coupled, then choose what one logical core task owns.
patterns.guardrails: Do not split true recurrence just to raise core count; do not leave independent orthogonal work serial without reason.
patterns.validate: Check low/high-work regimes, state ownership and tail/load imbalance.

patterns.title: Reason from physical layout/strides, not logical shape alone
patterns.decide: Identify physically contiguous axes and choose tile/copy orientation accordingly.
patterns.guardrails: A logical reshape/transpose is not free once contiguity/materialization is required.
patterns.validate: Cover non-aligned dimensions and all stride/layout forms allowed by the contract.

patterns.title: Avoid unnecessary full-tensor host materialization
patterns.decide: Prefer legal tail/stride-aware kernel handling when host pad/contiguous/transpose would copy full tensors.
patterns.guardrails: Do not move work into the kernel when the target API cannot express it efficiently or safely.
patterns.validate: Inspect/measure the full operator path and verify tail writes stay in bounds.

patterns.title: Keep runtime scheduling in Host Tiling and use only real regimes
patterns.decide: Derive block count, tiles, loops, internal mode keys, workspace and any small set of resource-driven regimes in Host Tiling/TilingData.
patterns.guardrails: Do not hard-code evaluator shapes or create public scheduling inputs.
patterns.validate: Check tiling-data ranges, ceil-div math and cases immediately below/at/above every regime boundary.

patterns.title: Design aligned full tiles and partial tails explicitly
patterns.decide: Keep the common full-tile path simple and isolate partial work behind legal mask/pad/tail-copy handling.
patterns.guardrails: Never read/write beyond the contract; do not make all tiles pay tail overhead unless required.
patterns.validate: Cover size 1 and alignment-1/alignment/alignment+1 plus representative large tails.

patterns.title: Place memory by lifetime, reuse distance and ownership
patterns.decide: List simultaneously live values and place persistent state, cross-stage exchange and scratch across registers/UB/L1/L0/workspace/GM.
patterns.guardrails: Do not alias overlapping lifetimes or multi-buffer data that has no asynchronous ownership hazard.
patterns.validate: Recompute budgets after tiling, fusion, buffering or dtype changes.

patterns.title: Separate persistent, cross-stage and scratch workspace
patterns.decide: Give long-lived state, producer-consumer exchange and short scratch separate ownership/reuse models.
patterns.guardrails: Do not use one maximal ring depth for all temporaries.
patterns.validate: Check offset/alignment, per-core/head ownership and overwrite distance.

patterns.title: Define storage, compute, accumulation and output precision
patterns.decide: For each stage record storage dtype, casts, compute dtype, accumulator dtype and any required operation order.
patterns.guardrails: Mathematical equivalence may not preserve signed zero, rounding, saturation or reduction order.
patterns.validate: Use required bitwise/tolerance checks and precision-sensitive values.

patterns.title: Choose padding/sentinel values from operation semantics
patterns.decide: Use the true neutral/sentinel for sum/max/min/mask/select and define NaN/Inf behavior only if the contract requires it.
patterns.guardrails: Zero is not a universal neutral value.
patterns.validate: Exercise partial tiles where padded lanes enter reductions/comparisons.

patterns.title: For elementwise/broadcast work, establish the data-movement skeleton first
patterns.decide: Choose the independent tile axis and broadcast staging for a simple GM->UB->Vector->GM correctness path before deeper pipelining.
patterns.guardrails: Do not over-engineer small kernels before workload evidence justifies it.
patterns.validate: Cover singleton broadcast axes, tails and low-work shapes.

patterns.title: For reductions, define ownership, accumulator semantics and full-data passes
patterns.decide: Choose complete-vs-partial reduction ownership, merge strategy, accumulator dtype/order and document baseline full-data pass count.
patterns.guardrails: Cross-core merges and online/pass-fused formulations change traffic and may change numerical order.
patterns.validate: Test small/large reduction lengths, tails, cancellation and extreme values.

patterns.title: For scan/recurrent work, keep carried state with its dependency chain
patterns.decide: Assign a complete state chain to one logical owner when feasible and parallelize independent batch/head/row/window axes around it.
patterns.guardrails: Avoid per-step cross-core state handoff unless the algorithm requires it.
patterns.validate: Test single/multi-step, final partial chunk and initial/final-state forms.

patterns.title: For sparse/paged/gather work, separate index semantics from staging
patterns.decide: Define legal index/page/chunk interpretation and output order before deciding coalescing or direct UB/L1 assembly.
patterns.guardrails: Do not reorder semantically ordered sparse entries for locality unless permitted.
patterns.validate: Cover minimal, adjacent/non-adjacent/repeated indices and boundary pages allowed by the contract.

patterns.title: For Cube work, choose resident and streaming operand roles
patterns.decide: Choose M/N/K ownership and which reused operand, if any, should remain resident while the other side streams through L1/L0.
patterns.guardrails: Residency must fit L1/L0 and must not destroy useful multicore parallelism.
patterns.validate: Check capacity, alignment, K tails and low-M/N occupancy regimes.

patterns.title: For mixed Cube/Vector work, define the producer-consumer protocol first
patterns.decide: Define producer, consumer, intermediate location, true-ready/reuse edges and maximum safe in-flight distance before choosing flags/rings/stage counts.
patterns.guardrails: Do not default to C-then-V lockstep or copy fixed credit/ring values from another kernel.
patterns.validate: Prove slot overwrite safety across prologue, steady state and drain.

patterns.title: Define asynchronous buffer ownership before queues/flags
patterns.decide: For each async CopyIn/compute/CopyOut or cross-core handoff, define who owns each buffer/slot and which event transfers ownership.
patterns.guardrails: A barrier may hide an ownership bug while serializing the pipeline.
patterns.validate: Check first iteration, steady state, final partial iteration/drain and slot reuse.

patterns.title: Specialize only real regimes and keep a generic fallback
patterns.decide: Use TilingKey/template specialization only for stable algorithm/resource/hardware-path differences.
patterns.guardrails: Do not specialize on evaluator case IDs or proliferate variants without reason.
patterns.validate: Test every specialization boundary plus a generic-only case.

patterns.title: Keep target-platform source separate from local validation adaptation
patterns.decide: Keep official target CANN/SOC implementation authoritative; constrain local adaptation to platform plumbing when possible.
patterns.guardrails: A local proxy must not become a second algorithm or be presented as target-platform proof.
patterns.validate: Target build uses official target configuration and local adaptation scope is auditable.

patterns.title: Build the correctness matrix from semantics/hardware boundaries and localize failures
patterns.decide: Cover modes, dtypes, optionals, smallest shapes, alignment/tails, representative/stress cases; classify failures before redesigning architecture.
patterns.guardrails: Do not weaken tolerance/reference/case coverage or stack speculative fixes.
patterns.validate: Record comparison mode and add the smallest regression case for each fixed failure.
